description: Fully responsive, interactive step-by-step walkthrough tool for solving linear equations with unknowns on both sides. Built with Singularity Design System (Poppins font, #4A4DC9 indigo / #FF7212 orange palette, pill buttons, geometric decorations). Covers Example 5 (11y + (–5) = 61, solvable) and Example 6 (6y + 7 = 4y + 21, unknowns on both sides). Supports verification, practice mode, real-world connections, and hands-on equation building using Brahmagupta's formula. Adapts to all screen sizes via container-based breakpoints (xs/sm/md/lg).
curriculum: NCERT Ganita Prakash Part-II, Chapter 7 - Finding the Unknown

teaching_notes: Guide students through this interactive tool. Start with Learn mode to walk through Example 5 (single-side unknown: 11y + (–5) = 61) and Example 6 (unknowns on both sides: 6y + 7 = 4y + 21). Encourage students to click 'Next Step' themselves and read each explanation. After solving, use the '✓ Verify' button to demonstrate substitution-based checking. In Practice mode, students solve equations independently — hints are available via the orange 'Hint' button. The Real World mode connects equations to weighing scales and the savings problem from the textbook. Hands On mode lets students build Ax + B = Cx + D equations and discover what happens when A = C (no solution or infinite solutions). The tool is fully responsive and works on student tablets, phones, and classroom projectors.
instructions_for_student: Collect unknown terms on one side and constants on the other. Use inverse operations: add/subtract to move terms, multiply/divide to isolate the variable. If unknowns cancel leaving a false statement (like 4 = 7), there is no solution. If they cancel leaving a true statement (like 5 = 5), there are infinite solutions. Always verify your solution by substituting back into the original equation!
